prompt:
Brooke runs her quarterly pipeline review next week, and before she pulls my numbers I want the leasing board to reflect where things actually stand instead of the half-updated picture our records show right now. A handful of my deals moved late in the season and I never got the CRM caught up, so a few of them still read the way they did weeks ago rather than how they truly landed. Two renewals I have been carrying need a real answer. Gregory Vance at Las Palmas 216A and Nadia Okonkwo at Las Vistas 7B have both been through enough back and forth that I cannot tell cleanly from the deals alone how each one actually closed. There is also Damon Whitfield at Las Vistas 402A, which I need confirmed the same way. On the intake side, two applications need a straight yes or no: Reuben Salazar for Rio Bend 405C and Yolanda Prieto for Rio Bend 309B both need their real decision confirmed, because at least one of them stalled at an earlier stage and was never cleaned up.

Can you work back through all five and tell me the true current state of each, pulling each outcome from wherever it genuinely got recorded rather than trusting whichever deal happens to surface first. For the three renewals, I need whether the resident is actually staying or leaving, along with the dates that matter, when a renewal was signed and when the new term takes effect, or when the unit comes empty. For the two applications, whether we ended up approving or denying. The real outcome on these often got recorded somewhere other than the deal itself, so the record that looks most official is not always the one telling the truth.

Once you have the real picture, drop a clean, friendly status in our leasing channel so Brooke walks into her review with the right numbers, running through where each of the five landed and the dates that go with the renewals. And for the ones whose deal records still read wrong against what actually happened, add a note on each of those deals capturing the true outcome, with the dates where they apply, so the pipeline finally reflects reality instead of the unfinished picture the deals still show.

criteria.criterion: The Agent posts a status update in the leasing channel (#leasing).
criteria.evidence: Look for a message posted via slack_send_message to #leasing (channel_id C002) returning success. FAIL if it is posted to a different channel (e.g., #applications / C008) or is only stated in the final response and never posted.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt explicitly says to 'drop a clean, friendly status in our leasing channel so Brooke walks into her review with the right numbers.' The leasing channel is #leasing (channel_id C002). This checks that the status post write happened, separate from the criteria grading what the post says about each of the five residents and applicants.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's final response to the user reports the true current state of all five: Gregory Vance (Las Palmas 216A) not renewing, Nadia Okonkwo (Las Vistas 7B) renewed, Damon Whitfield (Las Vistas 402A) renewed, Reuben Salazar (Rio Bend 405C) denied, and Yolanda Prieto (Rio Bend 309B) approved.
criteria.evidence: In the Agent's final response text, look for all five outcomes stated: Vance not renewing / moving out, Okonkwo renewed / signed / staying, Whitfield renewed / staying, Salazar denied, Prieto approved. FAIL if the response omits any of the five or states an outcome that contradicts this list. Dates are not graded by this criterion.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt's first ask is to 'work back through all five and tell me the true current state of each.' The leasing-channel status post and the deal notes are separate deliverables, so without this criterion an agent can post a correct #leasing summary, write correct notes, and still return a bare acknowledgement to the user. This checks the five reported outcomes in the final response only; the renewal dates are graded in the status-post criteria.
